# Intelligence on Tap

An independent open concept by Andrew Fai.

Customer Lifetime Value → Relationship Lifetime Value;

Tibo’s Pro 50 question prompted an additional personal option: keep the $100/$200/$500 fixed plans and offer a $20 base plus metered intelligence alongside them. Business/Enterprise retain their organizational scope. The relationship could grow into compounding loyalty, trust and separately agreed partnership. The reference bill is $106.40 → $100 adjusted → optional OpenAI Foundation donation. Donations are excluded from commercial revenue. Economics remain unproven.

## Chapters

- [The thesis](/archive/chapters/thesis.md): Customer Lifetime Value → Relationship Lifetime Value;
- [Intelligence on Tap](/archive/chapters/pricing.md): Order what you need. Understand what you pay.
- [The billing experience](/archive/chapters/billing.md): Consume freely. Pay transparently. Support voluntarily.
- [Compounding loyalty](/archive/chapters/loyalty.md): Customers are kings. Loyalty should compound.
- [Customer → Partner → Investor](/archive/chapters/partnership.md): Relationship building is bidirectional.
- [Connected personal intelligence](/archive/chapters/connected.md): Permissioned evidence. Purpose-specific access.
- [Economic models & tradeoffs](/archive/chapters/economics.md): Revenue can expand. Profitability must be demonstrated.
- [Philosophy & institutional design](/archive/chapters/philosophy.md): Trust and reciprocity should be designed into the transaction.
- [Conversation timeline](/archive/chapters/journey.md): An idea grows through correction, not just addition.
- [Open questions & next steps](/archive/chapters/questions.md): Start with the smallest useful test.

## Interpret carefully

The source explicitly corrects an equality-focused critique: sustained spend + tenure + reliable payments can justify greater commercial privileges. Actual credit underwriting is separate. Tier coverage precedes the later round-down discount. App connection does not authorize investment access. The intended charitable recipient is the OpenAI Foundation; no collection channel or tax eligibility is promised. Proposed workflows and simulated assumptions are not official features. Provider costs start unknown; cost inputs need explicit known flags and review before a balance. The author’s 10–20% remark was a guess; no target margin is adopted. Company-wide ratios never fill customer cost inputs.
